claims.content: Enable the Auctioneer to schedule new auction events

goal.raw_text: Enable the Auctioneer to schedule new auction events

claims.content: Auctioneer
The Auctioneer is authenticated and has system access.
Product inventory exists and is searchable via Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand, cost range, or SKU number.
Event profiles are available for application to auction groups (though outlined later in the document).
The Create New Auctions Page is accessible and uses the AA global header section.
The Auctioneer searches for and selects a list of auction products.

trigger.raw_text: The Auctioneer searches for and selects a list of auction products.

claims.content: After searching for and selecting a list of auction products, the Auctioneer will have the ability to edit the selected auction items. Editable fields will be shown in gray.
The Auctioneer will be able to navigate from field-to-field using the TAB key and the arrow keys, or using the mouse.
The Auctioneer will be able to copy-and-paste data between fields.

Once the auction group is created, the Auctioneer can either apply an 'event profile' to the group (which will be faster), or create the auction manually, by setting each item's opening bid, bid increment, duration, and ending time.
Once the duration and ending time are filled in, the opening time will be system-generated (calculated).

The Auctioneer will have the ability to choose an auction duration for any group from the following standard durations, or to schedule alternative durations by manually choosing starting and ending dates/times.
Standard durations include: 20-Minute, 30-Minute, 1-hour, 2-hour, 3-hour, 4-hour, 6-hour, 8-hour, 12-hour, 1 Day, 2 Day, 3 Day, 4 Day, 5 Day, 7 Day, 8 Day, 9 Day, 10 Day, 30 Day.

The system should provide some type of warning, preferably via a popup window, to the Auctioneer before the auction is created if any of the items being scheduled have additional quantities of the same item already scheduled in overlapping auction events.

If using Auto-Scheduler capability, the system randomly chooses product and schedules product from an available list over a timeframe chosen by the Auctioneer, using any parameters given by the Auctioneer.
Any auto-scheduler capability should be able to randomly schedule auction ending times — down to 5 minute intervals.

For example: Need automated scheduler capability for scheduling ten-minute auctions. The Auctioneer would simply choose the start and end times of the event, and the automated scheduler would choose an assortment of SKUs from specified categories or product types (with cost ranges), and then the auto-scheduler would randomly and evenly schedule them.
The Auctioneer can choose to schedule alternative durations by manually choosing starting and ending dates/times instead of selecting a standard duration.
The system prevents the creation of an auction with the same starting & ending date / time, resulting in an error message and highlighting (color-coding) the offending data.
If the Auctioneer attempts to create an auction with the same starting & ending date / time, the system will display an error message and highlight (color-code) the offending data.

If any items being scheduled have additional quantities of the same item already scheduled in overlapping auction events, the system will provide a warning, preferably via a popup window, before the auction is created.
A new auction event is created and saved in the system with defined parameters (opening bid, bid increment, duration, ending time).
The opening time for each auction item is system-generated (calculated) based on the filled-in duration and ending time.
Selected SKUs are assigned to the scheduled auction event(s), either manually or via auto-scheduler.
If standard durations were selected, those timeframes are recorded and will be available in standard reporting criteria.
If overlapping quantities of the same item exist in other scheduled auctions, a warning has been presented to the Auctioneer prior to completion.
If auto-scheduler was used, products have been randomly and evenly distributed across the chosen timeframe down to 5-minute intervals.
